entries.summary: k8s-test-env.sh accepts registry services with no Helm values override while still applying explicit values to those that have them.

entries.targetImpact: Opted-in Kubernetes targets retain explicit per-service --values arguments but no longer fail on services that omit values. Deployment order, health gates, and chart defaults are unchanged.

entries.summary: k8s-test-env.sh can finish one precisely identified interrupted Helm teardown whose labelled namespace and release are stuck uninstalling.
entries.why: HI-084: an interrupted teardown can leave an Active harness-labelled namespace with its only Helm release permanently uninstalling. Normal isolated runs must not reuse it, and recover-orphan correctly refuses it because the namespace still exists, so no bounded script-owned recovery path remained.
entries.targetImpact: Opted-in Kubernetes targets gain the exceptional cleanup-stuck-release command. It refuses mutation unless the current context, disposable namespace prefix, harness-loop-test=true/Active identity, release identity, and uninstalling status agree; only then it retries bounded Helm uninstall, deletes the namespace, and verifies both identities are absent. Normal deploy/test teardown is unchanged.
mergeActions: Refresh the Kubernetes environment tool and all three K8s workflow references together.
Use cleanup-stuck-release only with explicit human approval of the exact local/disposable context, release, and namespace; never broaden it into a prefix sweep or direct cluster-resource deletion.
verification: bash harness-loop/scripts/demo.sh proves a wrong context is rejected without mutation and the exact uninstalling release is uninstalled, its namespace deleted, and both identities independently absent

entries.summary: run-loop.mjs runs the baseline gate once per session (re-running only while red to confirm a repair), instead of every iteration.

entries.targetImpact: run-loop.mjs reuses a green baseline-state for subsequent iterations and re-runs only while red. The post-checker baseline re-run and the end-of-session feature replay are unchanged, so regression coverage is retained where it belongs.

entries.summary: `designer` and `design-reviewer` are retired and merged into one `design-facilitator` agent; the auto-reject loop between them is replaced by a human-authored `loop/design-approval.json`.
entries.why: designer/design-reviewer could reject and re-dispatch each other with no human in the loop, and a design that changed even slightly between rounds reset the one-bounded-retry escalation counter, so rejection could cycle indefinitely — every round a paid session, and neither agent had the business context to know when a design was actually done. Full incident: docs/reference/graph.md row 11.

entries.summary: Every writing agent's prompt (maker, checker, feature-planner, test-designer, test-implementer, harness-setup, design-facilitator, orchestrator) now closes with an explicit, uniformly-worded Yes/No reflection gate before it stops, instead of a one-off sentence phrased differently per agent. `test-implementer` previously had no closing memory guidance at all — that gap is now closed too.
entries.why: `docs/reference/agent-memory.md` already named the `stop` hook's moment as 'the natural place to also prompt' this question, but the hook itself can only run a shell command (it fired `trace.mjs`'s `session-end` event and nothing else) — it cannot force an honest self-assessment. The enforceable half of that intention was always the prompt text, and it existed per-agent as loose prose an agent could skim past inside a longer numbered list, phrased slightly differently every time, which made it easy to treat as one more instruction rather than a forced branch to actually answer.
entries.targetImpact: Each agent prompt's memory-writing instruction is now a literal two-branch question ('did this run produce something the next run shouldn't have to rediscover? Yes -> write an entry. No -> nothing to write') instead of a single conditional sentence. The underlying trigger criteria (a non-obvious mistake, an approach that worked for a non-obvious reason, an ambiguity that was hard to call, etc.) are unchanged per agent — only the framing is uniform. No hook or tool behavior changed.
mergeActions: If a target customized the closing memory paragraph of any of these prompts, port the customization's specific trigger criteria into the new Yes/No framing by hand — a mechanical diff would overwrite the customization.
No tool, hook, or schema changed; this is prompt text only.

entries.summary: approval-gate.mjs fires a best-effort OS notification the moment it writes a fresh approval request, so a headless run does not silently sit until timeout with nobody having seen it.
entries.why: Observed live: a headless run-loop.mjs sat at an approval gate with nobody watching that terminal. A safe timeout (APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MIN) prevents an infinite hang, but auto-rejecting on a timeout nobody saw still spends the judgement this gate exists to get.
entries.targetImpact: macOS uses osascript, Windows uses the built-in WinRT toast APIs (no extra module), Linux uses notify-send. HARNESS_NOTIFY=0 opts out; HARNESS_NOTIFY_CMD overrides with any `cmd title message`. A missing/broken notifier never blocks or fails the gate — it degrades to prior behavior.
mergeActions: Copy the updated approval-gate.mjs as-is; no schema or CLI flag changed, only an additive notify() call.

entries.summary: One feature's implementation step may now be built by several makers at once over disjoint file sets, with exactly one maker running the verification afterwards.
entries.why: WIP=1 bounds features, not files, so a step touching several independent modules was serialized for no reason — while the real hazard (two agents in one file, or two agents writing single-writer state) had no mechanical guard. tools/work-split.mjs supplies it: a plan is refused when its slices intersect by glob or on disk, when a slice reaches feature_list.json/progress.md/loop/**/memory/**, when a brief is too thin for a worker that has nobody to ask, or when the fan-in runs anything other than the feature's own verification.
entries.targetImpact: Optional capability; nothing changes for a target that never writes a plan. loop/route.mjs gains three implementation-layer rules and a mode field; the orchestrator gains one bounded exception to spawning a single child; the maker prompt gains slice-worker and integrator modes; guard-write.mjs confines a worker to its slice when HARNESS_SLICE is set; run-loop.mjs dispatches a fan-out headless (HARNESS_MAX_PARALLEL, default 4). Confinement is real only for workers started with loop/dispatch.mjs --slice on Claude Code or Codex; an in-session spawn cannot set per-child environment, and kiro has no PreToolUse hook at all.
mergeActions: Copy tools/work-split.mjs and create loop/work-split/ with its README; both are new, so no target content is at risk.

entries.summary: Four fixes drawn from reading every memory entry across the example projects: the memory schema is now checked, memory findings are grouped, duplicate detection compares bodies rather than exact wording, a blocked dependency is named where it dams open work, the review contract asks what a wrong implementation would still pass, and a prove feature whose own oracle is wrong finally has a node allowed to fix it.
entries.why: HI-068: agent-memory.md documents an entry frontmatter schema that nothing enforced, so on examples/jdt-mcp-server 61 of 71 entries had none, duplicate detection silently no-opped, memory-query.mjs returned '[?]' with empty hooks, and two maker entries five features apart recorded the identical root cause — the second costing a mutant round that read as 'all mutants survived'. The same tool emitted 66 identical warnings out of 68 findings, the wall AGENTS.md calls worse than no gate. HI-069: route.mjs's test-implementer rule keys on empty evidence, so a project that authors oracles before the implementation put every prove feature permanently out of the oracle layer's reach while the maker was forbidden to touch the test and the checker could not write it — no node could fix that file. HI-070: a blocked prove feature used as a stage gate turns its maxAttempts into the whole downstream branch's budget, and the only symptom was the router saying 'none routable'. HI-071: adversarialChecks had five keys and none asked the question a green run cannot answer for itself, which is what about twenty-five checker and maker memory entries are all separately about.
entries.targetImpact: memory-consolidate.mjs and environment.mjs gain findings/fields but change no behaviour a target depends on. loop/route.mjs gains one oracle-layer rule and a dependency-walk on the none-routable fallthrough. verify-harness.mjs gains the blocked-dependency-dam warn. tools/review-contract.mjs now REQUIRES adversarialChecks.discrimination as a sentence: any reviewPacket written before this upgrade becomes SUBMISSION_INCOMPLETE until the field is added, which is maker feedback and costs no checker attempt. The three prompts gain the NEEDS ORACLE FIX: contract.

entries.summary: Memory entries and index hooks are written in English, whatever language the rest of the project uses. Existing entries in another language stay as they are.
entries.why: Memory is not project prose: it is an operational record addressed to whichever agent runs next, in the same class as a log line or an identifier, and the reader is rarely the writer. A mixed-language index also costs the cheap skim the index exists to buy — examples/jdt-mcp-server had 43 of its index lines and 55 of its 81 entries in a second language. Deliberately a rule and not a gate: with the back catalogue frozen, a check would fire on 98 items forever with no action available, which is the wall AGENTS.md calls worse than no gate.
entries.targetImpact: Documentation only. references/agent-memory.md states the rule, and every memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md template repeats it where an agent will read it before writing. No existing entry is rewritten, and nothing fails because of one.
mergeActions: Refresh docs/reference/agent-memory.md; it is skill-owned.

Add the one-paragraph rule to each memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md header — those files are project content, so copy the paragraph rather than overwriting the file, and leave every existing index line untouched.

entries.summary: A project whose baseline gate is genuinely expensive may reuse a recorded green across sessions instead of re-running it.
entries.why: The gate already runs once per session, but every NEW session re-pays it in full even when nothing it reads has changed. Measured: jdt-mcp-server's provisioner replay costs 562 s per run because the clean-cache path really downloads a JDT LS distribution.
entries.targetImpact: loop/baseline-cache.mjs ships with every tree and stays inert until the project writes loop/baseline-cache.json. When enabled it digests the working tree by content plus declared toolchain probes; run-loop.mjs reuses a recorded green only on an identical digest inside the age limit, and every other outcome — no policy, no git, a red baseline, a missing or differing digest, a stale run — means run. baseline-state.json gains inputsDigest, reusedAt and reuseCount; checkedAt still records when the gate actually ran.
mergeActions: Refresh loop/run-loop.mjs and add loop/baseline-cache.mjs from the canonical template.
Leave the cache off unless the baseline is genuinely expensive; opting in means writing loop/baseline-cache.json with the project's own root, probes and ignore paths.

entries.summary: A repair turn — a red baseline, or a feature the checker already rejected — is routed only after its root cause is on record.
entries.why: A repair implemented against a guessed cause spends an attempt, edits production code and leaves the real cause in place. On examples/jdt-mcp-server a repeated EMFILE looked like a watcher defect; a standalone spike proved it was host directory-watch state, and the correct repair was to change nothing. Without that turn the loop would have patched production code to hide a host problem and the evidence would have looked green.
entries.targetImpact: route.mjs splits a repair in two. A red baseline with no recorded cause, and an eligible feature with attempts >= 1 and no cause recorded for that attempt, both route maker with mode: diagnose and layer: diagnosis. The diagnose turn writes loop/diagnosis/<key>.json keyed on the failure identity (baseline:<evidenceDigest> or <feat-id>#<attempts>); it is valid only with a non-empty symptom, cause, provedBy.cmd and at least one ruledOut entry. run-loop.mjs now records mode in route-log.jsonl and requestDispatched ignores diagnose rows, so the diagnose turn does not spend the one bounded repair turn. Features with attempts 0 are unaffected.
mergeActions: Refresh loop/route.mjs, loop/run-loop.mjs and loop/maker-prompt.md from the canonical template, and add loop/diagnosis/README.md.
Regenerate the agent files (node tools/gen-agents.mjs --target .) so the maker's diagnostician mode reaches every runtime.

entries.summary: A dispatch that returned nothing is retried with a jittered backoff; one that produced output stays terminal.
entries.why: All three runtimes fail in ordinary ways mid-session — a dropped connection, a spawn that never starts, an exit with no output — and every one of those killed a whole loop iteration. The pre-step gate (HUC-2026-08-29) only proves the runtime is driveable before the first turn.
entries.targetImpact: dispatch.mjs exports classify({spawnError, output, code}) returning {failure, retry, why}. TRANSPORT and EMPTY_RESPONSE retry; REFUSAL returns 75 as before; a non-zero exit that produced output returns that code unchanged, because the retry unit is an agent session that edits files and such a turn may have half-landed work. Budget HARNESS_DISPATCH_RETRIES (default 2, 0 disables), backoff 500ms doubling to a 10s cap with full jitter. dispatch() also accepts an AbortSignal that cancels the backoff. A spawn error now returns a classified non-zero code instead of throwing. No deadline: a hung dispatch still hangs, and bounding it needs process-group management that changes what Ctrl+C does.
mergeActions: Refresh loop/dispatch.mjs from the canonical template.
Set HARNESS_DISPATCH_RETRIES=0 in any environment where a re-dispatch is not acceptable.

entries.summary: The improvement backlog takes three producers instead of one, and a ranked issue can be routed into a feature list as work the loop cannot close by itself.
entries.why: The improve loop was fed only by verify-harness's static gates. trace-insights.mjs found real inefficiency in the loop's own behavior and wrote nothing down; a human correcting the loop had nowhere to put it; unverified assumptions were counted by nobody. Every one of those signals evaporated at the end of a session.
entries.targetImpact: trace-insights.mjs gains three human-signal detectors (router-escalation, approval-rejected, approval-unanswered) and one knowledge detector (open-unknowns, layer project), stamps every option with a stable trace/<id> signature and severity warn, and gains --report to write a trace-insights/1 artifact. harness-issue.mjs import accepts that schema alongside harness-verify/1 and filters layer=project from both; a new `feedback` command records a human correction under gate human. improve-harness.mjs --reverify now runs BOTH detectors per target and never auto-resolves a gate=human issue; a new --route writes the top-ranked issue into a feature_list.json as a feature whose verification is --reverify --id, so created work still cannot mark itself done.
mergeActions: Refresh tools/trace-insights.mjs from the canonical template; the backlog tools live in the skill and are not scaffolded.
Run `node tools/trace-insights.mjs --report` after a loop session, then import it into the skill backlog.

entries.summary: The workflow diagrams are split into onboarding, development and improvement, and a content-based gate fails when any of them falls behind the routing table.
entries.why: One file mixed three audiences and three moments, and nothing checked it. The existing graph-stale gate compares mtimes: it fires after any git checkout that rewrites two files in the same second, and stays silent when a rule really changes. Measured drift the new gate found on the shipped file: harness-setup was an agent nobody had drawn, and final-acceptance and baseline were rollback layers the router returns that no diagram named.
entries.targetImpact: references/workflow-diagram.md keeps its filename and becomes a map linking workflow-onboarding.md (Floor 1: requirement or existing repo to a green harness), workflow-development.md (Floor 2: green harness to DONE, including the per-iteration sequence and the K8s path) and workflow-improvement.md (the three-producer backlog and its closing rule). scripts/check-workflow-diagram.mjs reads agents.manifest.json and loop/route.mjs --rules and requires every agent, router node and rollback layer to appear inside a mermaid fence — prose does not count, and layers are matched through the LAYER: convention. verify-harness.mjs runs it as the docs-gate workflow-diagram-stale, opt-in on the diagrams being present, so scaffolded targets are unaffected.
mergeActions: The diagrams live in the skill and are not scaffolded — no target file changes.
Run node harness-loop/scripts/check-workflow-diagram.mjs after any change to route.mjs's rules or agents.manifest.json.

entries.summary: The router ignores blocked features when deciding whether test design is still missing.
entries.why: A blocked feature is an explicit stop. Sending test-designer back to it recreated stopped work and could keep unrelated eligible work from advancing.
entries.targetImpact: loop/route.mjs excludes status=blocked from both the missing-falsifier count and test-designer candidates. No state migration is required.
mergeActions: Refresh loop/route.mjs from the canonical template, preserving the target's real feature statuses and existing falsifier markers.
Rerun node loop/route.mjs to confirm an eligible feature, not a blocked one, is selected.

entries.summary: Maker and checker prompts live under prompts/, with manifest, coverage, verification and generated agents following that canonical location.
entries.why: The loop directory was mixing control-plane state with agent instructions. A single prompt home makes the runtime inputs discoverable and prevents the generator and coverage gates from silently following different paths.
entries.targetImpact: agents.manifest.json points maker and checker at prompts/maker.md and prompts/checker.md. The scaffold carries those prompt files; check-coverage.mjs, verify-harness.mjs and generated-agent tooling recognize the moved locations. Targets with custom prompts need a semantic merge, then regeneration; generated runtime files remain derived artifacts.
mergeActions: Move or semantically merge maker and checker prompt contents into prompts/, then update manifest prompt references.
Regenerate runtime agent files with node tools/gen-agents.mjs --target .; never hand-edit generated outputs.

entries.summary: After observing a feature newly reach done, the orchestrator reads run-report, trace-insights and trajectory, proposes at most one evidence-backed improvement, and routes it only after explicit human approval.
entries.why: Telemetry that is never read loses the cost of a completed feature; telemetry that edits the harness automatically turns an optimization heuristic into unsupervised scope change. The workflow needed both a mandatory retrospective and a human approval seam before implementation.
entries.targetImpact: The orchestrator prompt gains a post-done retrospective. It records a material lesson and proposal in its existing memory/handoff files, treats missing telemetry as unknown, and routes an approved project proposal to the planner or a canonical harness proposal through the issue/improvement pipeline. It never runs setup or --force as an upgrade.
mergeActions: Semantically merge the retrospective section into a customized orchestrator prompt; preserve project-specific instructions and keep the explicit human-approval gate.
Refresh the graph documentation and regenerate runtime agents from the merged manifest/prompt; never hand-edit generated agents.
For an existing target, use skills/harness-upgrade rather than setup --force.
